title: Rav Acha bar Yosef
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman criticizes Seder HaDorot for conflating two Amoraim who lived at different times and whose names also differ (for the first is always called Rav Acha bar Yosef and the second always Rav Acha son of Rav Yosef). The first, Rav Acha bar Yosef, was Rav Huna’s student and the uncle of Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, as in Shabbat 140a: Rav Acha bar Yosef (the Rif reads Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef, which Hyman considers a scribal error; in the Rif manuscript it is correct — Dikdukei Soferim) was walking leaning on the shoulder of Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, his sister’s son. He said to him: “When we reach Rav Safra’s house, bring me in.” When they arrived, he brought him in. He asked him … “Should the Master not also ask about a scarf?” He said to him: “About a scarf I have no question, for I asked Rav Huna and he resolved it for me.” Hyman concludes clearly from this that he was Rav Huna’s student, and in the days of Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak he was already very old.

He was likewise Rav Chisda’s student, as in the source designated ב״ה 87a, where he asked Rav Chisda, “Did we learn bread of legumes?” etc. (there it reads son of Rav Yosef, but Dikdukei Soferim reads bar Yosef); and in Chullin 105a he asked Rav Chisda, “The meat between the teeth — what is it?” In Eruvin 29b, “Rav Acha son of Rav Yosef thought to say before Rav Yosef” — Dikdukei Soferim truly reads “before Rav Ashi,” or Hyman suggests that it should read bar Yosef; and he sat with Rav Yosef, like all Rav Huna’s students, who afterward sat with Rabbah and Rav Yosef, who were heads of the academy in Pumbedita. Under the name Rav Acha bar Yosef he is mentioned in Shabbat 110b: he suffered from jaundice, and Rav Kahana made him a remedy and he was healed; and in Shabbat 140a he suffered from heaviness of the heart, and Mar Ukva healed him; he went and asked in the study house. But Rav Acha son of Rav Yosef was much later; he sat before Rav Ashi and always asked him, as in Yevamot 31a, Bava Metzia 42a, Menachot 35b and Niddah 69b. He was very sharp, as in Bava Metzia 109b, where he asked Rav Ashi, and he answered him: “When you reach the slaughtering of consecrated animals, come and raise difficulties for me” (Rashi explains: I recognized in you that you are sharp and know how to delve deep and raise difficulties). In Bava Metzia 77b he said to Rav Ashi: “But we say in Rava’s name”; and in Chullin 43a he said to Rav Ashi: “Thus we say in Mar Zutra’s name.” Hyman concludes from all this that he lived in Rav Ashi’s days, and everywhere he is called Rav Acha son of Rav Yosef.

notes.text: Returned Shabbat140a asks ABOUT a scarf, not FOR one, and reads heaviness of the HEART, דליבא, versus supplied דליכא. דרס/סוררא are read גרס/סודרא. The source’s כב״ה87a is retained as an unresolved tractate abbreviation in the body; saved Davidson BavaMetzia87a paragraph16 contains the bread/legumes question, providing a named matching locator instead of the draft’s BavaBatra guess. Hyman’s two-person distinction and alternatives remain arguments.

The consulted Shabbat 140a sequence explicitly names Acha leaning on his sister’s son Nachman bar Yitzchak, entering Safra’s house and asking about a scarf; he is not requesting one. The other passage reads heaviness of the heart. Hyman’s always-based two-figure distinction, Rif/manuscript and Ashi/Yosef alternatives remain attributed. Supplied כב״ה 87a remains unresolved alongside the current note’s named Bava Metzia match.
